10 Bamburi Cement Limited
Annual Report & Financial Statements 2015

Chairman’s Statement
2015 was a year of great strides for
the Group and it is my pleasure to
present another set of strong results
with outstanding achievements. Within
an improved operating environment in
the region, combined with our efforts,
we have witnessed better results
signalling continued good returns for
our shareholders.
Macro Economic Factors
Kenya continued to experience dynamic changes and
developments focussing on improving the lives and incomes of its
citizens through stable macroeconomic policies despite a volatile
global business environment, and investment in key sectors to
spur productivity and economic growth. The country hosted key
events such as the 10th World Trade Organisation Ministerial
Conference as well as high profile visits by world leaders, a
clear demonstration that the country was moving in the right
direction. Increased Government commitment and investment
in security restored confidence in foreign direct investment
while tourism showed signs of resurgence. The economy
grew above the Sub-Saharan average supported by lower
energy costs, investment in infrastructure, agriculture,
manufacturing and other industries, which fostered a
friendlier business environment with positive returns.
The macroeconomic environment remained robust
despite a few challenges. Real GDP growth stood
between 5.5% and 5.8% compared to 5.2% prior
year. Annual inflation increased to 8.01 % from 6.9%
in 2014 while exchange rates were impacted by
a stronger US dollar and weaker forex inflows.
Interest rates were fairly stable in the first half of
the year but rose in the third quarter due to higher
government paper yields. This, in turn, had a
negative impact on consumer borrowing resulting
in a slowdown in the construction industry with
the lag effect coming in the last quarter of the year.
But the CBK actions in the last quarter quickly
ensured macroeconomic stability.
